raw_response:
*Sits on a low stool, rolls a cigarette, thinks for a while before speaking.*

Aiya, what to say... I've been planting cotton on this little piece of land for longer than most people have been alive. 45 years. I don't know fancy rates and kilograms per this and that — I just do what works, what I've always done, what the old folks taught me and what I've learned from the land itself.

**About the land and us.** Four and a half mu, all cotton, like most households on this side of the county. It's just me and my old lady now — our son went to Shijiazhuang years ago, sends money sometimes but doesn't come back for picking anymore. Two old people, 4.5 mu of cotton — that's about what we can handle, and even that is getting hard. My back isn't what it was.

**Plowing and planting.** I don't have my own tractor, never did. Around Qingming is too early, the ground's still cold. I wait till the end of April, when the poplar leaves come out — that's the sign. A few days before planting I call Old Wang with his tractor, he does my field together with a few neighbors, 40 yuan per mu. For seed I go to the agricultural shop in town, buy whatever packet they're selling this year — some hybrid thing, I can't read the name but the young clerk tells me it's the same one everyone's buying. About 50, 60 yuan per mu for seed. Nobody saves cotton seed around here anymore.

**Fertilizer.** Before I plow I spread compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind, one bag per mu. That's four and a half bags for my land. Then when the cotton starts squaring, around end of June, I put down urea — about 15 kg per mu, broadcast by hand while I'm hoeing. If the leaves still look pale I might add a little more at flowering, but usually not — urea is more than 100 yuan a bag now, I can't keep dumping it on. My neighbor Old Zhao uses more than me, his cotton is greener, but he's also spending more and I don't know if he comes out ahead.

**Water.** I share the well with three other households. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat does, thank heavens. I water twice — once when the buds are forming in early July, once in early August when the bolls are filling. If it rains good in July I might skip one. The pump electricity adds up, maybe 30-40 yuan each time per mu.

**Pests.** Cotton without spraying, there's no cotton — the bollworms will strip it bare. I spray four or five times through summer. I walk through the field every few days and look at the leaves and the squares. When I see worms or the damage, I go to the shop, show them what I've got, they sell me a bottle. I mix it in the sprayer on my back. Aphids too, early in the season. I don't know what all the chemicals are called — I just trust what the shop gives me.

**Picking.** That's the hardest part, and it only gets harder each year. We start first picking mid-September, then again early October, then the last pick late October. Three rounds. My wife and I pick together, slow, maybe 30-40 jin a day each when we're fresh. Some of the bigger households hire pickers — 100 yuan a day now, plus meals. We can't afford that. We just take longer.

**What I expect.** Last year was alright, I sold about 1000 jin of seed cotton total — that came out to maybe 240 jin of lint per mu after ginning, so around 120 kg per mu lint. Wait — I think in seed cotton, not lint. Let me say it plain: I expect maybe 500 jin per mu of seed cotton, which the buyer converts. If the weather is decent and the bollworms don't go crazy.

**My worry this year.** Cotton price has been flat for years. Input prices keep climbing. I keep doing it because I don't know what else to do on this land, and we eat from what I sell. If I were younger I might try something else — some folks are doing vegetables — but I'm 65 and tired, and I know cotton.
